LESSON: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFT - BEADWORK

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.10: Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can beadwork be used to preserve Kenyan culture?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss function of jewellery in Kenyan communities
2. identify materials for beadwork in the local environment
3. sing a patriotic song adorned in beaded jewellery inspired by patriotism
4. recognise beadwork as an indigenous Kenyan craft

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFT - BEADWORK
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFT - BEADWORK
Study Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Discuss function of jewellery in Kenyan communities

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss function of jewellery in Kenyan communities. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss function of jewellery in Kenyan communities.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss function of jewellery in Kenyan communities. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify materials for beadwork in the local environment

What this means
In this part you learn to identify materials for beadwork in the local environment. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify materials for beadwork in the local environment.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify materials for beadwork in the local environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Sing a patriotic song adorned in beaded jewellery inspired by patriotism

What this means
In this part you learn to sing a patriotic song adorned in beaded jewellery inspired by patriotism. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: sing a patriotic song adorned in beaded jewellery inspired by patriotism.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can sing a patriotic song adorned in beaded jewellery inspired by patriotism. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Recognise beadwork as an indigenous Kenyan craft

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise beadwork as an indigenous Kenyan craft. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise beadwork as an indigenous Kenyan craft.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise beadwork as an indigenous Kenyan craft. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: discuss function of jewellery in Kenyan communities)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork in your own words. (skill: identify materials for beadwork in the local environment)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: sing a patriotic song adorned in beaded jewellery inspired by patriotism)

Example 4: Show how “Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: recognise beadwork as an indigenous Kenyan craft)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: discuss function of jewellery in Kenyan communities.
3. Practise this skill: identify materials for beadwork in the local environment.
4. Practise this skill: sing a patriotic song adorned in beaded jewellery inspired by patriotism.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can beadwork be used to preserve Kenyan culture?
2. How can you express patriotism through Creative activities?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Indigenous Kenyan Craft - Beadwork means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: discuss function of jewellery in Kenyan communities.
5. Be able to: identify materials for beadwork in the local environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
